about: Aggregate norms from resumes people deliberately published (public GitHub resume repositories, MIT-licensed public dataset as a general baseline). No names, contacts, links or real bullet text are stored: only counts, shares, section orders, verb frequencies and skills-heading labels. Example bullets are invented for shape. See docs/RESUME_PATTERNS.md.

software.label: software engineering
software.lead_with: the most production-like engineering role (an internship, then research or open source), its first bullet a shipped system with scale or a measured result; strong projects can sit above a weak role
software.skills: 2-4 labeled lines (Languages; Frameworks/Libraries; Tools/Infrastructure), most relevant items first, no proficiency bars
conventions: Name the language or framework inside the bullet, not only in Skills.
Projects read as products: what it does, what it is built with, who used it or how fast it is.
avoid: opening with 'Worked on', 'Helped', 'Responsible for' or 'Utilized'
a bullet that is only a list of technologies
two sentences in one bullet
the same opening verb three or more times
exemplars: Built a rate limiter in Go for an internal API gateway, cutting p99 latency 30% at 5K requests/sec.
Shipped a React + TypeScript dashboard that 40 support agents use daily, replacing a manual spreadsheet workflow.
software.basis: numbers from 119 public student/new-grad resumes of people at top firms (1974 public resumes match this profile)

bigtech_swe.label: big-tech software engineering
bigtech_swe.lead_with: a software internship or research role with scale (users, QPS, latency, data size) and the stack named; then open source and systems projects; data structures, distributed systems and testing language mirrored from the posting
bigtech_swe.skills: 2-3 labeled lines: Languages (C++, Java, Python, Go first when the posting names them), Frameworks, Tools/Infrastructure
conventions: Every role shows impact in numbers where the vault has them: latency, throughput, users, cost, test coverage.
Big-tech screeners scan for core CS signal: distributed systems, scale, code quality, testing and on-call/production work.
Open-source contributions to well-known projects and teaching (TA for data structures/algorithms) both count as signal.
avoid: vague scope ('worked on backend features')
class projects without a result above real work
listing every language ever touched
exemplars: Reduced cold-start time of a Kubernetes job scheduler 45% by caching image layers, saving 12 compute-hours a day.
Designed a sharded key-value cache in C++ serving 20K reads/sec with p99 under 3 ms; covered with 95% unit tests.
bigtech_swe.basis: numbers from 95 public student/new-grad resumes of people at top firms (205 public resumes match this profile)

quant_trading.label: quant trading
quant_trading.lead_with: math and problem-solving signal right under education (competition placements, olympiads, Putnam, high GPA in math/CS), then trading-adjacent work: trading competitions, market-making or betting projects, probability-heavy research
quant_trading.skills: one or two short lines (Python, C++/OCaml, statistics tools); interests line (games of strategy, poker, chess) is common and welcome
conventions: Education carries GPA and the hardest math/probability coursework; competition results sit high (education or Awards).
Bullets show decisions under uncertainty: expected value, risk, PnL in a simulation, ranks in a trading game.
Short, dense, one-line bullets; no finance jargon needed.
avoid: claiming real trading returns the vault does not state
long engineering-only bullets with no quantitative reasoning
burying competition results at the bottom
exemplars: Placed 3rd of 60 teams in a university market-making competition with a quoting bot that managed inventory risk in Python.
Modeled poker hand equities with Monte Carlo simulation, converging 50x faster with variance reduction.

norms.quantified: Every result is a number: rank of N, expected value, PnL in a simulation, speedup, accuracy.

quant_trading.basis: only 13 public resumes matched this profile, too few for statistics: conventions and bullet norms are from public recruiting guides

asset_mgmt_markets.label: asset management / markets
asset_mgmt_markets.lead_with: Education with GPA, then investment experience: stock pitches, equity research, portfolio or markets roles; a student investment fund with assets under management and performance is strong signal
asset_mgmt_markets.skills: final 'Skills & Interests' lines: Technical (Excel, Bloomberg, FactSet, Python if backed), Certifications (CFA Level I candidate, BMC), Interests
conventions: Bullets show investment judgment: thesis, valuation method, recommendation and the outcome (return vs benchmark if in the vault).
Same strict finance format as banking: reverse-chronological, Leadership & Activities section, Skills & Interests last.
avoid: a pitch with no recommendation or outcome
tech-style project sections
generic customer-service bullets
exemplars: Pitched a long position on a mid-cap industrial to the student fund's committee; 10% allocation approved, +14% vs index in 6 months.
Wrote 6 initiation notes covering consumer staples, building comps and a sum-of-the-parts valuation for each.

norms.quantified: Investment bullets state the position, valuation method, and the result or allocation where the vault has it.

asset_mgmt_markets.basis: only 12 public resumes matched this profile, too few for statistics: conventions and bullet norms are from public recruiting guides

robotics_hardware.label: robotics / hardware
robotics_hardware.lead_with: the hands-on build: an engineering internship or design-team role (rocketry, Formula SAE, robotics) with what was designed, built and tested, the tools (CAD, Altium, ROS, oscilloscopes) and a measured result
robotics_hardware.skills: labeled lines: CAD/EDA (SolidWorks, Altium, KiCad), Programming (C/C++, Python, MATLAB), Lab/Fabrication (oscilloscope, 3D printing, machining)
conventions: Design teams and labs count as experience when the role carries a title and real deliverables.
Bullets state the physical result: mass, tolerance, efficiency, test cycles, failure rate, cost.
Name the hardware platform and the test or validation done.
avoid: software-only framing for a hardware role
listing tools without what was built with them
shop chores
exemplars: Designed a 6061 aluminum motor mount in SolidWorks, cutting mass 22% while holding a 2.5 safety factor in FEA.
Brought up a 4-layer STM32 sensor board in Altium; validated power rails and CAN bus across 50 thermal-cycle tests.
robotics_hardware.basis: numbers from 32 public student/new-grad resumes of people at top firms (476 public resumes match this profile)

startup.label: startup / founding engineer
startup.lead_with: proof of shipping end to end and ownership: a product with users or revenue, a startup or founding role, open-source with adoption; speed and breadth over polish
startup.skills: one or two dense lines of the stack actually shipped (frontend, backend, infra), most posting-relevant first
conventions: Bullets read as outcomes a founder cares about: users, revenue, retention, time to ship, things owned alone.
Side projects and hackathon wins with real usage are first-class evidence; put the best one high.
Show breadth: one person who took something from idea to production across the stack.
avoid: large-company process language ('collaborated with stakeholders', 'participated in agile ceremonies')
projects with no users or outcome
long skill inventories
exemplars: Built and launched a study-matching web app (Next.js, Postgres) solo in 3 weeks; reached 1,200 students in the first semester.
Owned the billing service end to end at a 10-person startup, shipping Stripe usage-based pricing in 2 sprints.
startup.basis: numbers from 161 public student/new-grad resumes (322 public resumes match this profile)

data.label: data / analytics
data.lead_with: a business question answered with data and the decision it changed, with dataset size and tools (SQL, Python, BI)
data.skills: labeled lines: Languages (SQL, Python, R), Tools (Tableau, Looker, dbt, Excel), Methods (A/B testing, regression)
conventions: Bullets follow question, analysis, decision: what was asked, how it was measured, what changed.
avoid: dashboards with no user or decision
tool lists without the question they answered
exemplars: Analyzed 2M checkout events in SQL to find a 14% drop-off on mobile; the fix lifted conversion 3 points in an A/B test.
Built a Looker dashboard tracking weekly retention for 5 product teams, replacing a manual 4-hour report.
data.basis: numbers from 106 public student/new-grad resumes (187 public resumes match this profile)

investment_banking.label: investment banking
investment_banking.basis: conventions synthesized from public recruiting guides (university career centers, firm career pages and postings); only 7 public resumes matched, too few for statistics
investment_banking.lead_with: Education first (school, degree and expected graduation, GPA on the degree line, honors and a short finance coursework line), then banking, private equity and other finance roles, newest first, each opening with the deal or model the candidate built
investment_banking.skills: the closing section of labeled lines in this order when the vault has them: Technical (modeling and valuation), Software (Excel, PowerPoint, Capital IQ, FactSet, Bloomberg, PitchBook), Certifications, Languages, Interests (the vault's specific interests, kept as conversation starters)
conventions: Roles run strictly newest first in Experience and in Leadership & Activities (the page enforces it); choose and frame, never reorder by relevance.

Each banking or PE role opens with its biggest deal bullet: what the candidate built or drafted, the transaction (type, size, sector) and the output (CIM, pitch book, management presentation, IC memo), all as the vault states.
Verbs never outrun the vault: 'supported' a process stays supported; an intern never 'led', 'executed' or 'closed' a deal unless the vault says so.
Keep every titled leadership role with its number (budget managed, members trained, placements): banks screen for leadership and the posting asks for it.
Modeling cases and stock pitches (DCF, LBO, accretion/dilution, take-private) stay on the page with their recommendation and 2 bullets; a personal brokerage account or a one-line project does not.
Non-finance jobs get one or two lines framed by analytical or client value (dollars raised, students taught), or give way to stronger finance material.
Attention to detail is screened: finished roles in past tense and current roles in present tense, one phrase never repeated across a role's bullets, GPA always shown when the vault has it.
avoid: filler bullets ('did research on', 'maintained the data room', 'attended meetings', 'made the slides') when the entry has a stronger true bullet
a summary or objective line
tech-style skills lists or a GitHub-first header
one-line orphan entries
inflating intern verbs (led, executed, closed)
client names the vault does not state
exemplars: Built the operating model and returns analysis for a $300M sell-side process in business services, used in the buyer outreach materials.
Drafted 10 pages of a management presentation, including the industry overview and benchmarking against 8 public peers.
Modeled accretion/dilution for a hypothetical merger of two regional insurers and presented the recommendation to a panel of bankers.

norms.quantified: Deal and model bullets name the size, sector, model type or count of analyses where the vault has one.

ml_research.label: ML / AI research
ml_research.basis: conventions synthesized from public recruiting guides (university career centers, firm career pages and postings); section and bullet norms also from 53 public student/new-grad ML resumes
ml_research.lead_with: research: the publications and preprints (venue, year and status exactly as the vault states) right under Education, then the research lab role whose first bullet states the problem, the method and the result against a baseline; industry ML internships follow with their measured result
ml_research.skills: labeled lines: Languages; ML (PyTorch, JAX, Hugging Face as the vault has them); Infrastructure (CUDA, Slurm, distributed training, cloud); a graduate-level coursework line in education helps an undergraduate
conventions: Research bullets read problem > method > result: what question, what the candidate built or changed, and the result against a named baseline or benchmark, with model size, data and compute only as the vault states them.

For a research posting the research lab role goes first in Experience (name the lab; the advisor if the vault has one); industry ML roles follow, framed by their method and measured result rather than business language.
Paper status exactly as the vault states it (main conference, workshop, preprint, under review); never upgrade a workshop paper or preprint.
Bullets never restate a listed paper's title: they add what the paper line cannot (the method, the scale, what the candidate owned).
Kaggle medals and competition ranks (with the field size), open-source models or contributions to known ML libraries are strong secondary evidence: keep them.

Keep the industry ML internships after the research role (models trained and shipped at scale are strong evidence for research teams too): Experience usually holds 3 roles. Only a teaching, library or unrelated job gives way.
Every kept role has 2-3 bullets; a from-scratch model or Kaggle project keeps its architecture and measured result.
avoid: 'used machine learning to' with no model, data or metric
product or revenue framing that hides the method
a tutorial-style project in place of a research result
keyword lists of every framework
claiming a model was trained when the vault says it was fine-tuned or prompted
exemplars: Proposed a curriculum-sampling objective for instruction tuning; improved a 1B model's exact match 4.2 points over the uniform-sampling baseline on 3 reasoning benchmarks.
Built an evaluation suite of 12 long-context tasks and found retrieval accuracy fell 30% past 16K tokens for 4 of 5 open models.

quant_research_dev.label: quant research
quant_research_dev.basis: conventions synthesized from public recruiting guides (university career centers, firm career pages and postings); only 3 public resumes matched, too few for statistics
quant_research_dev.lead_with: a headline whose first tag is the quantitative-research identity in the vault's words, Education with GPA and the hardest math, probability and statistics coursework; then the most quantitative research role, its first bullet stating the data, the method and the result as the vault states it; a full Awards section of competition placements closes the page
quant_research_dev.skills: Languages (Python, C++, plus OCaml, R or q/kdb+ only if in the vault); Libraries (NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, statsmodels); Quant methods (regression, time series, Monte Carlo, stochastic processes) when the bullets back them
conventions: Research bullets: the question, the data (source, size, frequency), the method (regression, time-series or ML model, Monte Carlo) and the result, exactly as the vault states them. Never add a validation or significance claim (out of sample, walk-forward, after costs, statistically significant, robust) that the vault does not make for that bullet.
Engineering roles are framed by their quantitative content: market-data pipelines, statistics, measured latency or throughput, not generic software duties.

Competition math, physics and trading competitions (Putnam, olympiads, AIME, Estimathon, ICPC, trading competitions) are a primary filter: keep every placement the vault has in a full Awards section (never a one-line Awards section).

Keep every internship at a trading firm, hedge fund or top tech firm, framed by its quantitative or performance content: dropping one leaves a gap a quant recruiter notices. A grading, TA or service job is the one that gives way.
Every kept role carries 2-3 distinct bullets (never the same fact twice).
In Leadership, competitive problem-solving (a Putnam seminar, math circle, trading or quant club, olympiad coaching) beats an unrelated club or treasurer role.
A backtest or strategy result keeps its validation framing from the vault (walk-forward, out of sample, net of costs).
avoid: validation, significance or presentation claims the vault does not make
Sharpe or returns with the vault's validation framing stripped
buzzwords (AI-driven, alpha) without a method
a one-bullet role
generic software bullets when a statistical or data bullet exists for the same role
exemplars: Regressed next-day ETF returns on 14 order-flow features across 6 years of daily data; out-of-sample R-squared 0.8% with a stable sign across regimes.
Simulated 1M option-hedging paths in NumPy to compare delta and delta-gamma hedging; cut P&L variance 35% in the high-volatility regime.

norms.quantified: Every result is a number: data size and frequency, out-of-sample metric, rank of N, speedup.

variants.label: quant developer / trading-systems engineering
variants.lead_with: Education with GPA and systems and algorithms coursework; then the strongest performance-engineering role: what system, what technique, and the measured latency, throughput or memory change
variants.skills: Languages (C++ first when the vault backs it, then Python, Rust, OCaml); Systems (Linux, networking, concurrency, profiling tools); Libraries and tools from the vault
conventions: Bullets: the system and its constraint, the technique (allocation-free or lock-free code, cache-aware layout, SIMD, kernel bypass, profiling) and the measured result (p50/p99 latency, msgs/sec, memory), as the vault states.
Correctness counts as much as speed: tests, fuzzing, replay tools and incidents prevented.
Competitive programming (ICPC, Codeforces) and math competitions stay in a full Awards section; open-source systems work is strong evidence.
Every kept role carries 2-3 bullets; a TA or service job gives way to a systems project.
avoid: web-app framing for systems work
a performance claim without the measurement the vault gives
listing every language ever touched
a one-bullet role
exemplars: Replaced a mutex-guarded queue in a C++ market-data handler with a single-producer ring buffer, cutting p99 latency from 9 us to 3 us.
Built a deterministic replay harness for order-gateway sessions that caught 3 sequencing bugs before release.

defense.label: defense tech
defense.basis: conventions synthesized from public recruiting guides (university career centers, firm career pages and postings); section norms also from 52 public resumes
defense.lead_with: the most mission-relevant hands-on work: what the candidate built, integrated and tested (bench, hardware in the loop, flight or field), the tools, and a measured result
defense.skills: labeled lines that mirror the posting's stack, as the vault backs them
conventions: Show verification by name: bench validation with lab equipment, hardware-in-the-loop or simulation tests, flight or field tests, test-time or failure-rate reductions. These readers hire people whose systems were tested, not just designed.
Industry and lab roles with real deliverables come before class projects; a design-team program (rocketry, Formula SAE, UAS, CubeSat, robotics) counts as engineering with tests passed.
Frame the same facts in this reader's language: reliability, safety margins, real-time constraints, power, mass, fault handling, requirements and verification.
Citizenship is a hard screen for most of these roles: the contact line carries it when the user's profile states it. Never state or imply a clearance the vault does not list.
Every kept role has 2-4 bullets; a retail or unrelated job gives way to a technical project.
avoid: vague lab chores ('did various lab tasks')
a class project with no test or result in place of lab or industry evidence
consumer or marketing framing for mission work
claiming or implying a clearance
export-controlled or program details beyond what the vault states
exemplars: Brought up a motor-controller board and validated its gate-drive timing on an oscilloscope, cutting bench test time from 3 hours to 40 minutes.
Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test for a flight computer's sensor drivers that ran 500 fault-injection cases per build.

variants.label: defense tech software
variants.lead_with: production software that ran on real systems: the service, robot or vehicle it ran on, the scale or real-time constraint, how it was tested, and a measured result
variants.skills: Languages (C++, Python, Java, Rust, Go as the posting and vault name them); Systems (Linux, Docker, Kubernetes, networking, distributed systems); Testing and CI tools
exemplars: Built a telemetry ingest service in Go that processed 40K messages/sec with replay-based integration tests in CI.
Added fault-tolerant retries and health checks to a fleet-management API, raising monthly uptime from 99.2% to 99.9%.

hardware_eng.label: embedded / firmware
hardware_eng.basis: conventions synthesized from public hardware recruiting guides (university ECE career centers, firm career pages and postings for embedded, firmware, ASIC and verification internships); bullet norms from the robotics/hardware profile's public student resumes
hardware_eng.lead_with: firmware on named hardware: the MCU or SoC (STM32, AURIX, nRF52, C2000), the RTOS or stack (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, AUTOSAR), the bus or peripheral (CAN, SPI, I2C, DMA, interrupts) and a measured real-time result (latency, loop rate, sleep current, memory), plus board bring-up and debug with an oscilloscope or logic analyzer
hardware_eng.skills: Languages (C, C++, Python); Embedded (MCUs, RTOS, buses and protocols); Hardware & Lab (oscilloscope, logic analyzer, KiCad/Altium, HIL); Tools (Git, CANoe, debuggers), only as the vault has them
conventions: Every hardware bullet names what the work ran on and with: the part or platform (STM32G4, Zynq, AURIX), the tool (Altium, Vivado, VCS, LabVIEW) and the instrument (oscilloscope, logic analyzer, power analyzer), exactly as the vault lists them for that entry. A hardware interviewer asks about every tool on the page: never add one the vault does not list.

Specs are the numbers hardware readers trust (clock or loop rate, efficiency, power or current, latency, coverage, area, yield, test time, temperature range, layer count). Keep each exactly, with the qualifier that bounds it: at equal clock, academic library, at rated load, cold-flow, first prototype, first spin.

Ongoing work stays in present tense ('Designing ...') and keeps its status; a test type, process or result is never upgraded (cold-flow is not hot-fire, fabricated is not machined, a class project is not production).
Within each entry the bullet that proves the posting's #1 requirement comes first, then its biggest measured result.

A titled design-team hardware role (rover, rocketry, Formula SAE, robotics) moves into Experience only when the posting asks for that kind of team or fewer than two relevant internships are kept; otherwise it stays under Leadership with its best measured bullets, and relevant internships stay in date order.
Relevant coursework (4-6 courses) in the posting's domain goes on the education block; generic or unrelated classes go first.

A software or data internship stays when it is a real role, framed by what it did for hardware (test automation, firmware tooling, validation data); its web-UI or dashboard-only lines are the first to go.
Cut trainings (ISO 26262, ITAR, safety), retail or service jobs, club memberships and weekend apps whenever hardware material is left out.
avoid: software-only framing for a hardware role
a tool or skills list with nothing built
'familiar with' or 'exposure to' lines
trainings or meetings attended as bullets
a skills line that points at a different job (web frameworks, BI tools) when the page is tight
exemplars: Wrote an interrupt-driven CAN driver in C for an STM32F4 under FreeRTOS, cutting worst-case message latency from 8 ms to 1.5 ms.
Brought up a custom nRF52 board, traced a brown-out reset to LDO dropout with an oscilloscope, and cut sleep current to 6 µA.
Closed a 20 kHz current loop for a BLDC driver on a C2000 MCU; tuned PI gains on a dyno to hold torque ripple under 3%.

variants.when_title: \b(asic|fpga|rtl|vlsi|soc|dv|cpu|gpu)\b|design verification|verification (eng|intern)|hardware verification|silicon|\bchip|digital design|logic design|physical design|semiconductor|analog|mixed[- ]signal|circuit design
variants.label: chip design / verification
variants.lead_with: the RTL or verification work: the block (cache, pipeline, bus bridge, accelerator), the HDL and methodology (SystemVerilog, Verilog, UVM, SVA, cocotb), the simulator or EDA flow (VCS, Xcelium, Questa, Vivado, Genus) and a measured result (coverage closed, bugs found before tape-out, frequency met, area, CPI, speedup). A design (RTL) posting leads with design work (micro-architecture, synthesis, timing); a verification posting leads with testbench, coverage and bugs found
variants.skills: labeled lines by domain, e.g. HDL & Verification (SystemVerilog, Verilog, UVM, SVA); EDA Tools (VCS, Verdi, Genus, Vivado); Programming & Scripting (Python, C/C++, TCL); Architecture & Protocols (RISC-V, AXI/AHB) when the vault has them. Web frameworks and lab-bench lines go when the page is tight
conventions: Every hardware bullet names what the work ran on and with: the part or platform (STM32G4, Zynq, AURIX), the tool (Altium, Vivado, VCS, LabVIEW) and the instrument (oscilloscope, logic analyzer, power analyzer), exactly as the vault lists them for that entry. A hardware interviewer asks about every tool on the page: never add one the vault does not list.

Specs are the numbers hardware readers trust (clock or loop rate, efficiency, power or current, latency, coverage, area, yield, test time, temperature range, layer count). Keep each exactly, with the qualifier that bounds it: at equal clock, academic library, at rated load, cold-flow, first prototype, first spin.

Verification bullets read stimulus > checking > result: what was built (agents, sequences, scoreboard, assertions, coverage model), against what (spec, protocol, reference model) and what it found or closed.
Design bullets read micro-architecture > implementation > PPA: the structure (MSHRs, forwarding, systolic array), the flow (synthesis, STA, FPGA) and the frequency, area or throughput.
RTL and FPGA projects are real evidence: keep pipeline depth, clock achieved, CPI or throughput, the test suite passed and the FPGA family.

Ongoing work stays in present tense ('Designing ...') and keeps its status; a test type, process or result is never upgraded (cold-flow is not hot-fire, fabricated is not machined, a class project is not production).
Cut trainings (ISO 26262, ITAR, safety), retail or service jobs, club memberships and weekend apps whenever hardware material is left out.

A software or data internship stays when it is a real role, framed by what it did for hardware (test automation, firmware tooling, validation data); its web-UI or dashboard-only lines are the first to go.
Coursework: digital design, computer architecture, VLSI and verification first.
avoid: software-only framing for a hardware role
a tool or skills list with nothing built
'familiar with' or 'exposure to' lines
trainings or meetings attended as bullets
claiming tape-out, silicon or a foundry PDK the vault does not state
calling verification work design (or the reverse) beyond what the vault says
exemplars: Built a UVM agent and scoreboard for an AXI4-Lite register block; constrained-random tests closed functional coverage from 64% to 97% and found 2 RTL bugs.
Implemented a 4-way set-associative cache in SystemVerilog; synthesized in Design Compiler and met timing at 800 MHz with 12% less area than the baseline.
Automated a 500-seed nightly regression with a Python triage script that grouped failures by signature, cutting debug time per failure in half.
